cells.tense: Here, with the pen, you can hold a new thing steady while it is still soft.
cells.act: share your strength where it is needed
cells.ask: Choose the beginning here that is still rough, give it an hour of what you are good at, and stop when the hour is up.
cells.core:
You know how to stand where something ends without flinching. When a thing is over, you are already at the clearing — no sentiment about it, and none about the bare ground either. That steadiness is real, and it is yours. You let things finish.

The other half is giving that steadiness to something small. There is a beginning here that has not taken shape yet, and what you are good at is exactly what it needs to get a first form. One start, one hour, done. It takes time you would otherwise spend watching the old thing be gone. What you get back is a piece in your hand that exists now because you stood there and put your weight behind it.
cells.sheetLine: You can stand on bare ground and start something small.
cells.verb: Holding the first piece of a thing that is about to exist
cells.place: The cleared ground where something has fully ended and the next thing has not started

cells.tense: You will keep the ground open so nothing has to be settled, and the next start will stay unmade.
cells.act: name every feeling in it on one page, none of them crossed out
cells.ask: Take a beginning you keep postponing, put every feeling about it on a single page, and leave all of them standing.
cells.core:
You are braced for what comes after the ending, and from where you stand the ground is still not settled. The old thing is gone, but you keep the space ready — and you keep each new start unmade, because an unmade thing can still be perfect. That is the trap. What stays possible does not have to be judged, and it also does not exist.

Here is what the record suggests instead. Feel it all the way, not only the clean part. Put every feeling about one of those beginnings on a single page — the excitement, the dread, the grief for what ended — and leave every one of them where it is. What you will have is the whole of it, visible at once, and that is what lets it begin.
cells.sheetLine: You keep it unmade so it can't fail.

cells.tense: The ending happened, and part of you is still standing in the doorway, writing it in present tense.
cells.act: look at the whole of it until nothing is left to see
cells.ask: Take what ended and go over all of it until there is nothing left you have not seen, then stop looking.
cells.core:
Part of you is still writing the ending as though it is happening now — the past in present tense. That is not sentiment. Looking all the way at something finished is harder than standing at the edge of it. The knack for beginnings is in you. Right now it is running low.

Start with seeing. Take what ended and go over all of it — not the version you can defend, the whole one, until nothing is left you have not seen. You will know when you are done. What you are after is not a verdict. It is finished seeing. That is what lets you turn around, and turning around is how the next stretch of ground comes into view.
cells.sheetLine: You are still writing an ending in present tense.

cells.tense: You have been clearing ground and starting things the whole time, and the story has no place where your name went.
cells.act: see it whole, with nothing hidden
cells.ask: Think of a start here you have not counted, look at all of it plainly, and write the steps on paper in your own words.
cells.core:
Look at what is around you and what changed. Some of it changed because of you — a thing ended, ground got cleared, something small got started — and you do not count that as your doing. It gets filed under timing, or circumstances, or someone else needing the space at the right moment. That is the part you have left out.

See it plainly. Take a start or an ending here that you have not counted, all of it, every step you actually took, and put it somewhere you can read it back. No credit language, no humility either. Just what you did. Seeing it whole is what puts your hand back on the pen, and the ground you cleared here already knows whose work it was.
cells.sheetLine: The ground you cleared was cleared by you.
